  <requirement id="R49">

    <spec_quote>interface AnimationPlaybackEvent : Event</spec_quote>

    <spec_quote>constructor(DOMString type, optional AnimationPlaybackEventInit eventInitDict = {});</spec_quote>

  <requirement id="R70">

    <spec_quote>readonly attribute double? currentTime;</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R71">
    <category>Existence</category>
    <description>AnimationPlaybackEvent must expose a readonly nullable timelineTime attribute.</description>
    <spec_quote>readonly attribute double? timelineTime;</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R72">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Each Document must have a unique default document timeline (exposed via document.timeline) with an origin time of zero that persists for the lifetime of the document, including across calls to document.open().</description>
    <spec_quote>Each `Document` has a [document timeline](#document-timeline) called the
default document timeline.
The [default document timeline](#document-default-document-timeline) is unique to each document
and persists for the lifetime of the document,
including calls to document.open() [[HTML]](#biblio-html "HTML Standard").

The [default document timeline](#document-default-document-timeline) has an [origin time](#origin-time) of zero.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R73">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Constructing a DocumentTimeline must create a document timeline associated with the Document of the current global Window, calculating its currentTime as a fixed offset (defined by the originTime option, defaulting to 0) from the timestamp provided during animation frame updates.</description>
    <spec_quote>`DocumentTimeline (options)`
:   Creates a new `DocumentTimeline`.
    The `Document` with which the timeline is associated
    is the `Document` associated
    with the `Window` that is the current global object.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R74">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Once a document timeline becomes active, its reported currentTime must be monotonically increasing.</description>
    <spec_quote>After a [document timeline](#document-timeline) becomes [active](#active-timeline),
it is [monotonically increasing](#monotonically-increasing-timeline).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R75">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>During the update animations and send events procedure for a document, a microtask checkpoint must be performed after updating timelines and removing replaced animations and before dispatching queued animation events, so promise callbacks run prior to event listeners.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. [Remove replaced animations](#remove-replaced-animations) for doc.
3. Perform a microtask checkpoint.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R76">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When dispatching queued animation events during an animation frame, the user agent must stably sort events by scheduled event time (with unresolved times sorting before resolved times) and then by composite order for equal scheduled event times.</description>
    <spec_quote>6. Perform a stable sort of the [animation events](#animation-events) in events to dispatch
   as follows:

   1. Sort the events by their [scheduled event time](#scheduled-event-time)
      such that events that were scheduled to occur earlier
      sort before events scheduled to occur later,
      and events whose scheduled event time is [unresolved](#unresolved)
      sort before events with a resolved
      scheduled event time.
   2. Within events with equal [scheduled event times](#scheduled-event-time),
      sort by their [composite order](#animation-composite-order).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R77">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Constructing an Animation(effect, timeline) must associate the animation with the provided timeline (or the current Window document's default document timeline if omitted) and set its associated effect to the provided effect.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. Let animation be a new `Animation` object.
    2. Run the procedure to [set the timeline of an animation](#animation-set-the-timeline-of-an-animation)
       on animation
       passing timeline as the new timeline;
       or, if the timeline argument is missing,
       passing the [default document timeline](#document-default-document-timeline)
       of the `Document` associated
       with the `Window` that is the current global object.
    3. Run the procedure to [set the associated effect of an animation](#animation-set-the-associated-effect-of-an-animation)
       on animation
       passing source as the new effect.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R78">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Calling Element.animate(keyframes, options) must construct a KeyframeEffect targeting the element, construct an Animation associated with the specified timeline (or the element's node document's default document timeline), assign the id option if provided, play the animation with auto-rewind enabled, and return the Animation.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. Let target be the object on which this method was called.
    2. Construct a new `KeyframeEffect` object effect
       in the relevant Realm of target
       by using the same procedure as the
       `KeyframeEffect(target, keyframes, options)` constructor,
       passing target as the target argument,
       and the keyframes and options arguments as supplied.

       If the above procedure causes an exception to be thrown,
       propagate the exception and abort this procedure.
    3. If options is a `KeyframeAnimationOptions` object,
       let timeline be the `timeline` member of options
       or, if `timeline` member of options is missing,
       the [default document timeline](#document-default-document-timeline) of the node document
       of the element on which this method was called.
    4. Construct a new `Animation` object, animation,
       in the relevant Realm of target
       by using the same procedure as the `Animation()` constructor,
       passing effect and timeline as arguments of the same name.
    5. If options is a `KeyframeAnimationOptions` object,
       assign the value of the `id` member of options
       to animation’s `id` attribute.
    6. Run the procedure to [play an animation](#play-an-animation) for animation
       with the auto-rewind flag set to true.
    7. Return animation.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R79">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>An animation's currentTime must return its hold time if resolved, null if there is no active timeline or start time is unresolved, and otherwise (timeline time - start time) * playback rate.</description>
    <spec_quote>If the animation’s [hold time](#animation-hold-time) is [resolved](#unresolved),
:   The [current time](#animation-current-time) is the animation’s [hold time](#animation-hold-time).

If *any* of the following are true: * the animation has no associated [timeline](#timeline), or * the associated [timeline](#timeline) is [inactive](#inactive-timeline), or * the animation’s [start time](#animation-start-time) is [unresolved](#unresolved),
:   The [current time](#animation-current-time) is an [unresolved](#unresolved) time value.

Otherwise,
:   > `current time =
    > (timeline time − start time)
    > × playback rate`</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R80">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Setting an animation's timeline to a different timeline must update the associated timeline, make hold time unresolved if start time is resolved, and update the animation's finished state.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. Let the [timeline](#timeline) of animation be
   new timeline.
4. If the [start time](#animation-start-time) of animation is [resolved](#unresolved),
   make animation’s [hold time](#animation-hold-time) unresolved.

   Note: This step ensures that the [finished play state](#play-state-finished) of animation
   is not “sticky”,
   but is re-evaluated based on its updated [current time](#animation-current-time).
5. Run the procedure to
   [update an animation’s finished state](#update-an-animations-finished-state) for animation
   with the did seek flag set to false,
   and the synchronously notify flag set to false.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R81">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Assigning an AnimationEffect that is already associated with another animation to a new animation's effect attribute must first disassociate the effect from the previous animation by setting the previous animation's effect to null.</description>
    <spec_quote>5. If new effect is not `null`
   and if new effect is the [associated effect](#animation-associated-effect)
   of another [animation](#concept-animation), previous animation,
   run the procedure to [set the associated effect of an animation](#animation-set-the-associated-effect-of-an-animation)
   (this procedure)
   on previous animation,
   passing null as new effect.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R82">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Setting animation.currentTime must seek a running animation (with resolved start time, unresolved hold time, active timeline, and non-zero playback rate) by setting startTime to timeline time - (seek time / playback rate), and otherwise must set its hold time to seek time.</description>
    <spec_quote>If *any* of the following conditions are true: * animation’s [hold time](#animation-hold-time) is [resolved](#unresolved), or * animation’s [start time](#animation-start-time) is [unresolved](#unresolved), or * animation has no associated [timeline](#timeline) or the associated timeline is [inactive](#inactive-timeline), or * animation’s [playback rate](#playback-rate) is 0,
   :   Set animation’s [hold time](#animation-hold-time) to seek time.

   Otherwise,
   :   Set animation’s [start time](#animation-start-time) to the result of evaluating
       `timeline time − (seek time / playback rate)`
       where timeline time is the current [time value](#time-value)
       of the [timeline](#timeline) associated with animation.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R83">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Setting animation.currentTime while the animation has a pending pause task must synchronously complete the pause by setting hold time to seek time, applying any pending playback rate, clearing start time, canceling the pending pause task, and resolving the ready promise with the animation.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. If animation has a [pending pause task](#pending-pause-task),
   synchronously complete the pause operation
   by performing the following steps:

   1. Set animation’s [hold time](#animation-hold-time) to seek time.
   2. [Apply any pending playback rate](#apply-any-pending-playback-rate) to animation.
   3. Make animation’s [start time](#animation-start-time) [unresolved](#unresolved).
   4. Cancel the [pending pause task](#pending-pause-task).
   5. Resolve
      animation’s [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise)
      with animation.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R84">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Setting animation.startTime must apply any pending playback rate, set start time, clear hold time when the new start time is resolved and playback rate is non-zero (or preserve previous current time as hold time when set to null), and cancel any pending play or pause task while resolving the ready promise with the animation.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. [Apply any pending playback rate](#apply-any-pending-playback-rate) on animation.
5. Set animation’s [start time](#animation-start-time) to new start time.
6. Update animation’s [hold time](#animation-hold-time) based on
   the first matching condition from the following:

   If new start time is [resolved](#unresolved),
   :   If animation’s [playback rate](#playback-rate) is not zero,
       make animation’s [hold time](#animation-hold-time) [unresolved](#unresolved).

   Otherwise (new start time is [unresolved](#unresolved)),
   :   Set animation’s [hold time](#animation-hold-time) to previous current time
       even if previous current time is [unresolved](#unresolved).
7. If animation has a [pending play task](#pending-play-task) or a [pending pause task](#pending-pause-task),
   cancel that task and resolve
   animation’s [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise)
   with animation.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R85">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>An animation's ready promise must initially be a resolved Promise fulfilled with the animation itself, and must be replaced with a new Promise whenever a pending play or pause task is queued while no pending task exists.</description>
    <spec_quote>The [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise) is initially a resolved Promise
created using the procedure to create a new resolved Promise
with the animation itself as its value
and created in the relevant Realm of the animation.

The object is replaced with a new Promise object
every time the animation queues
a [pending play task](#pending-play-task) or a [pending pause task](#pending-pause-task)
when it previously did not have a pending task,
or when the animation is canceled</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R86">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Calling animation.play() must auto-rewind currentTime to 0 when effective playback rate is non-negative and currentTime is unresolved, negative, or at or past associated effect end, or rewind to associated effect end when effective playback rate is negative and currentTime is unresolved, less than or equal to zero, or past associated effect end.</description>
    <spec_quote>If animation’s [effective playback rate](#effective-playback-rate) ≥ 0, and animation’s [current time](#animation-current-time) is *either*: * [unresolved](#unresolved), or * less than zero, or * greater than or equal to [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end),
   :   Set seek time to zero.

   If animation’s [effective playback rate](#effective-playback-rate) < 0, and animation’s [current time](#animation-current-time) is *either*: * [unresolved](#unresolved), or * less than or equal to zero, or * greater than [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end),
   :   If [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end) is positive infinity,
       :   throw an "`InvalidStateError`" `DOMException`
           and abort these steps.

       Otherwise,
       :   Set seek time to animation’s [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R87">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>The pending play task scheduled by animation.play() must execute asynchronously and must never be performed synchronously.</description>
    <spec_quote>If a user agent determines that animation is immediately [ready](#ready),
    it may schedule the above task as a microtask
    such that it runs at the next microtask checkpoint,
    but it *must not* perform the task synchronously.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R88">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When a pending play task runs with a resolved hold time, it must apply any pending playback rate, set start time to ready time - hold time / playback rate (or ready time if playback rate is 0), and clear hold time when playback rate is non-zero.</description>
    <spec_quote>If animation’s [hold time](#animation-hold-time) is [resolved](#unresolved),
       :   1. [Apply any pending playback rate](#apply-any-pending-playback-rate) on animation.
           2. Let new start time be the result of evaluating
              `ready time − hold time
              / playback rate`
              for animation.
              If the [playback rate](#playback-rate) is zero,
              let new start time be simply ready time.
           3. Set the [start time](#animation-start-time) of animation to new start time.
           4. If animation’s [playback rate](#playback-rate) is not 0,
              make animation’s [hold time](#animation-hold-time) [unresolved](#unresolved).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R89">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When a pending play task completes, it must resolve the animation's ready promise with the animation before running the procedure to update the animation's finished state.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. Resolve animation’s [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise)
       with animation.
    5. Run the procedure to [update an animation’s finished state](#update-an-animations-finished-state)
       for animation
       with the did seek flag set to false,
       and the synchronously notify flag set to false.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R90">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When the pending pause task scheduled by animation.pause() runs, it must set hold time to (ready time - start time) * playback rate if start time is resolved and hold time is unresolved, apply any pending playback rate, make start time unresolved, and resolve the ready promise with the animation.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. If animation’s [start time](#animation-start-time) is [resolved](#unresolved)
       and its [hold time](#animation-hold-time) is *not* resolved,
       let animation’s hold time be the result of evaluating
       `(ready time − start time)
       × playback rate`.

       Note: The [hold time](#animation-hold-time) might be already set
       if the animation is [finished](#play-state-finished),
       or if the animation has a [pending play task](#pending-play-task).
       In either case we want to preserve the hold time
       as we enter the [paused](#play-state-paused) state.
    3. [Apply any pending playback rate](#apply-any-pending-playback-rate) on animation.
    4. Make animation’s [start time](#animation-start-time) unresolved.
    5. Resolve animation’s [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise)
       with animation.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R91">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>The pending pause task scheduled by animation.pause() must run asynchronously.</description>
    <spec_quote>As with the [pending play task](#pending-play-task),
    the user agent must run the [pending pause task](#pending-pause-task) asynchronously,
    although that could be as soon as the next
    microtask checkpoint.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R92">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>During normal playback without seeking, when an animation with positive playback rate reaches or passes associated effect end, its hold time must be clamped to max(previous current time, associated effect end); when playback rate is negative and it reaches or passes 0, its hold time must be clamped to min(previous current time, 0).</description>
    <spec_quote>If [playback rate](#playback-rate) > 0 and unconstrained current time is greater than or equal to [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end),
   :   If did seek is true,
       let the [hold time](#animation-hold-time) be the value of unconstrained current time.

       If did seek is false,
       let the [hold time](#animation-hold-time) be the maximum value
       of [previous current time](#previous-current-time) and [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end).
       If the previous current time is [unresolved](#unresolved),
       let the hold time be associated effect end.

   If [playback rate](#playback-rate) < 0 and unconstrained current time is less than or equal to 0,
   :   If did seek is true,
       let the [hold time](#animation-hold-time) be the value of unconstrained current time.

       If did seek is false,
       let the [hold time](#animation-hold-time) be the minimum value
       of [previous current time](#previous-current-time) and zero.
       If the previous current time is [unresolved](#unresolved),
       let the hold time be zero.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R93">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When an animation enters the finished state (and remains finished when finish notification runs), its finished promise must be resolved with the animation and a finish AnimationPlaybackEvent with the animation's currentTime and timeline's currentTime must be queued.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If animation’s [play state](#animation-play-state)
         is not equal to [finished](#play-state-finished),
         abort these steps.
      2. Resolve
         animation’s [current finished promise](#current-finished-promise) object
         with animation.
      3. Create
         an `AnimationPlaybackEvent`, finishEvent.
      4. Set finishEvent’s `type` attribute
         to [finish](#finish-event).
      5. Set finishEvent’s `currentTime` attribute
         to the [current time](#animation-current-time) of animation.
      6. Set finishEvent’s `timelineTime` attribute
         to the [current time](#timeline-current-time)
         of the [timeline](#timeline) with which animation is associated.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R94">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When an animation leaves the finished play state after its finished promise has already resolved, its finished promise must be replaced with a new pending Promise.</description>
    <spec_quote>6. If current finished state is false
   and animation’s [current finished promise](#current-finished-promise) is already resolved,
   set animation’s current finished promise to
   a new promise in the relevant Realm of animation.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R95">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Calling animation.finish() must apply any pending playback rate, seek to associated effect end (if playbackRate > 0) or 0 (if playbackRate < 0), establish startTime if unresolved on an active timeline, cancel pending play/pause tasks and resolve ready, and synchronously resolve the finished promise and queue the finish event.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. [Apply any pending playback rate](#apply-any-pending-playback-rate) to animation.
3. Set limit as follows:

   If [playback rate](#playback-rate) > 0,
   :   Let limit be [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end).

   Otherwise,
   :   Let limit be zero.
4. [Silently set the current time](#animation-silently-set-the-current-time) to limit.
5. If animation’s [start time](#animation-start-time) is [unresolved](#unresolved)
   and animation has an associated [active timeline](#active-timeline),
   let the start time be the result of evaluating
   `timeline time
   − (limit / playback rate)`
   where timeline time is the current [time value](#time-value)
   of the associated [timeline](#timeline).
6. If there is a [pending pause task](#pending-pause-task)
   and [start time](#animation-start-time) is [resolved](#unresolved),

   1. Let the [hold time](#animation-hold-time) be [unresolved](#unresolved).

      Note: Typically the [hold time](#animation-hold-time) will already be unresolved
      except in the case when
      the animation was previously [idle](#play-state-idle).
   2. Cancel the [pending pause task](#pending-pause-task).
   3. Resolve the [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise)
      of animation with animation.
7. If there is a [pending play task](#pending-play-task)
   and [start time](#animation-start-time) is [resolved](#unresolved),
   cancel that task and resolve
   the [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise) of animation
   with animation.
8. Run the procedure to [update an animation’s finished state](#update-an-animations-finished-state)
   for animation
   with the did seek flag set to true,
   and the synchronously notify flag set to true.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R96">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Calling animation.cancel() on a non-idle animation must reset pending tasks, reject the finished promise with an AbortError DOMException and replace it with a new pending promise, queue a cancel AnimationPlaybackEvent with currentTime set to null, and make hold time and start time unresolved.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If animation’s [play state](#animation-play-state) is *not* [idle](#play-state-idle),
   perform the following steps:

   1. Run the procedure to [reset an animation’s pending tasks](#animation-reset-an-animations-pending-tasks)
      on animation.
   2. Reject the [current finished promise](#current-finished-promise)
      with a `DOMException` named "`AbortError`".
   3. Set the [[PromiseIsHandled]] internal slot
      of the [current finished promise](#current-finished-promise)
      to true.
   4. Let [current finished promise](#current-finished-promise) be
      a new promise in the relevant Realm of animation.
   5. Create
      an `AnimationPlaybackEvent`, cancelEvent.
   6. Set cancelEvent’s `type` attribute
      to [cancel](#cancel-event).
   7. Set cancelEvent’s `currentTime`
      to `null`.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R97">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Setting animation.playbackRate must synchronously clear any pending playback rate, update playbackRate, and preserve currentTime on a monotonically increasing timeline when currentTime was resolved.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. Clear any [pending playback rate](#pending-playback-rate) on animation.
2. Let previous time be
   the value of the [current time](#animation-current-time) of animation
   before changing the [playback rate](#playback-rate).
3. Let previous playback rate be
   the current [effective playback rate](#effective-playback-rate) of animation.
4. Set the [playback rate](#playback-rate) to new playback rate.
5. Perform the steps corresponding to
   the *first* matching condition from the following, if any:

   If animation is associated with a [monotonically increasing](#monotonically-increasing-timeline) [timeline](#timeline) and the previous time is [resolved](#unresolved),
   :   [Set the current time](#animation-set-the-current-time) of animation to previous time.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R98">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Calling animation.updatePlaybackRate(rate) must set the pending playback rate and apply it immediately if the animation is idle, paused, or has an unresolved currentTime, recalculate startTime and apply it immediately if finished, or asynchronously synchronize via play (without auto-rewind) if running.</description>
    <spec_quote>If previous play state is [idle](#play-state-idle) or [paused](#play-state-paused), or animation’s [current time](#animation-current-time) is [unresolved](#unresolved),
   :   [Apply any pending playback rate](#apply-any-pending-playback-rate) on animation.

       Note: The second condition above is required
       so that if we have a [running](#play-state-running) animation
       with an unresolved current time
       and no pending play task,
       we do not attempt to play it below.

   If previous play state is [finished](#play-state-finished),
   :   1. Let the unconstrained current time be
          the result of calculating
          the [current time](#animation-current-time) of animation
          substituting an [unresolved](#unresolved) time value
          for the [hold time](#animation-hold-time).
       2. Let animation’s [start time](#animation-start-time) be
          the result of evaluating the following expression:

          > `timeline time
          > − (unconstrained current time
          > / pending playback rate)`

          Where timeline time is the current [time value](#time-value) of
          the [timeline](#timeline) associated with animation.

          If [pending playback rate](#pending-playback-rate) is zero,
          let animation’s [start time](#animation-start-time) be timeline time.
       3. [Apply any pending playback rate](#apply-any-pending-playback-rate) on animation.
       4. Run the procedure to [update an animation’s finished state](#update-an-animations-finished-state)
          for animation
          with the did seek flag set to false,
          and the synchronously notify flag set to false.

   Otherwise,
   :   Run the procedure to [play an animation](#play-an-animation) for animation
       with the auto-rewind flag set to false.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R99">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Calling animation.reverse() on an animation with an active timeline must invert its effective playback rate as the pending playback rate and play the animation with auto-rewind enabled.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. Let animation’s [pending playback rate](#pending-playback-rate) be
   the additive inverse of its [effective playback rate](#effective-playback-rate)
   (i.e. `-effective playback rate`).
4. Run the steps to [play an animation](#play-an-animation) for animation
   with the auto-rewind flag set to true.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R100">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>animation.playState must evaluate to "idle", "paused", "finished", or "running" according to the first matching condition on currentTime, startTime, pending tasks, and playback range boundaries.</description>
    <spec_quote>*All* of the following conditions are true: * The [current time](#animation-current-time) of animation is [unresolved](#unresolved), *and* * the [start time](#animation-start-time) of animation is [unresolved](#unresolved), *and* * animation does *not* have *either* a [pending play task](#pending-play-task) *or* a [pending pause task](#pending-pause-task),
:   → idle

*Either* of the following conditions are true: * animation has a [pending pause task](#pending-pause-task), *or* * *both* the [start time](#animation-start-time) of animation is [unresolved](#unresolved) *and* it does *not* have a [pending play task](#pending-play-task),
:   → paused

For animation, [current time](#animation-current-time) is resolved and *either* of the following conditions are true: * animation’s [effective playback rate](#effective-playback-rate) > 0 and [current time](#animation-current-time) ≥ [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end); *or* * animation’s [effective playback rate](#effective-playback-rate) < 0 and [current time](#animation-current-time) ≤ 0,
:   → finished

Otherwise,
:   → running</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R101">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>animation.pending must return true if and only if the animation has a pending play task or a pending pause task.</description>
    <spec_quote>`pending`, of type boolean, readonly
:   Returns true if this animation has
    a [pending play task](#pending-play-task) or a [pending pause task](#pending-pause-task).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R102">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>An animation effect's activeDuration must be calculated as iteration duration * iteration count, or 0 if either iteration duration or iteration count is zero.</description>
    <spec_quote>> [active duration](#active-duration) =
> `iteration duration × iteration count`

If either the [iteration duration](#iteration-duration) or [iteration count](#iteration-count) are zero,
the [active duration](#active-duration) is zero.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R103">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>An animation effect's endTime must be calculated as max(start delay + active duration + end delay, 0).</description>
    <spec_quote>The end time,
of an [animation effect](#animation-effect)
is the result of evaluating
`max(start delay + active duration + end delay, 0)`.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R104">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>An animation effect's active time must equal local time - start delay during the active phase, max(local time - start delay, 0) in the before phase only when fill mode is backwards or both, max(min(local time - start delay, active duration), 0) in the after phase only when fill mode is forwards or both, and unresolved otherwise.</description>
    <spec_quote>If the animation effect is in the [before phase](#animation-effect-before-phase),
:   The result depends on the first matching condition from the following:

    If the [fill mode](#fill-mode) is [backwards](#fill-mode-backwards) or [both](#fill-mode-both),
    :   Return the result of evaluating
        `max(local time − start delay, 0)`.

    Otherwise,
    :   Return an [unresolved](#unresolved) [time value](#time-value).

If the animation effect is in the [active phase](#animation-effect-active-phase),
:   Return the result of evaluating
    `local time − start delay`.

If the animation effect is in the [after phase](#animation-effect-after-phase),
:   The result depends on the first matching condition from the following:

    If the [fill mode](#fill-mode) is [forwards](#fill-mode-forwards) or [both](#fill-mode-both),
    :   Return the result of evaluating
        `max(min(local time − start delay,
        active duration),
        0)`.

    Otherwise,
    :   Return an [unresolved](#unresolved) [time value](#time-value).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R105">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>An animation effect's overall progress must be calculated as (active time / iteration duration) + iteration start (or 0 + iteration start in the before phase and iteration count + iteration start otherwise when iteration duration is 0).</description>
    <spec_quote>If the [iteration duration](#iteration-duration) is zero,
   :   If the animation effect is in the [before phase](#animation-effect-before-phase),
       let overall progress be zero;
       otherwise, let it be equal to the [iteration count](#iteration-count).

   Otherwise,
   :   Let overall progress be the result of calculating
       `active time / iteration duration`.
3. Return the result of calculating
   `overall progress + iteration start`.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R106">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>An animation effect's simple iteration progress must be overall progress % 1.0 (or iteration start % 1.0 when overall progress is infinity), except it must become 1.0 when the modulo result is 0, the effect is in the active or after phase, active time equals active duration, and iteration count is non-zero.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. If [overall progress](#overall-progress) is infinity,
   let the simple iteration progress be
   `iteration start % 1.0`;
   otherwise,
   let the simple iteration progress be
   `overall progress % 1.0`.
3. If *all* of the following conditions are true:

   * the simple iteration progress calculated above is zero,
     *and*
   * the animation effect is in the [active phase](#animation-effect-active-phase)
     *or* the [after phase](#animation-effect-after-phase),
     *and*
   * the [active time](#active-time) is equal to the [active duration](#active-duration),
     *and*
   * the [iteration count](#iteration-count) is *not* equal to zero.

   Let the simple iteration progress be 1.0.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R107">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>An animation effect's directed progress must apply the playback direction (normal, reverse, alternate, alternate-reverse) so forwards iterations return simple iteration progress and reverse iterations return 1.0 - simple iteration progress.</description>
    <spec_quote>If [playback direction](#playback-direction) is [normal](#playback-direction-normal),
   :   Let the current direction be forwards.

   If [playback direction](#playback-direction) is [reverse](#playback-direction-reverse),
   :   Let the current direction be reverse.

   Otherwise (the [playback direction](#playback-direction) is [alternate](#playback-direction-alternate) or [alternate-reverse](#playback-direction-alternate-reverse))p,
   :   1. Let d be the [current iteration index](#current-iteration-index).
       2. If [playback direction](#playback-direction) is [alternate-reverse](#playback-direction-alternate-reverse)
          increment d by 1.
       3. If `d % 2 == 0`,
          let the current direction be forwards;
          otherwise let the current direction be reverse.
          If d is infinity,
          let the current direction be forwards.
3. If the current direction is forwards
   then return the [simple iteration progress](#simple-iteration-progress).

   Otherwise, return
   `1.0 − simple iteration progress`.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R108">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>An animation effect's transformed progress (returned as progress in getComputedTiming()) must evaluate the effect easing function with directed progress and the before flag set when in the before phase going forwards or in the after phase going backwards.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. The before flag is set
      if the animation effect is in the [before phase](#animation-effect-before-phase)
      and going forwards is true;
      or if the animation effect is in the [after phase](#animation-effect-after-phase)
      and going forwards is false.
3. Return the result of evaluating
   the [effect easing function](#animation-effect-effect-easing-function)
   passing [directed progress](#directed-progress) as the input progress value
   and before flag as the before flag.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R109">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>AnimationEffect.getComputedTiming() must resolve an "auto" duration to 0 and an "auto" fill to "none", whereas AnimationEffect.getTiming() must return the specified "auto" values.</description>
    <spec_quote>* `duration` –
      while `getTiming()` can return
      the string `auto`,
      `getComputedTiming()` must return
      a number corresponding to
      the calculated value of the [iteration duration](#iteration-duration)
      as defined in the description of
      the `duration` member of the `EffectTiming` interface.

      In this level of the specification, that simply means that an
      `auto` value is replaced by zero.
    * `fill` –
      likewise, while `getTiming()` can return
      the string `auto`,
      `getComputedTiming()` must return
      the specific `FillMode` used for timing calculations
      as defined in the description of
      the `fill` member of the `EffectTiming` interface.

      In this level of the specification,
      that simply means that an `auto` value is replaced
      by the `none` `FillMode`.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R110">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Calling AnimationEffect.updateTiming(timing) must update only the timing properties present in the input dictionary without modifying omitted properties, and must update the associated animation's finished state.</description>
    <spec_quote>5. Assign each member that exists in input
   to the corresponding timing property of effect as follows:

   * `delay` → [start delay](#start-delay)
   * `endDelay` → [end delay](#end-delay)
   * `fill` → [fill mode](#fill-mode)
   * `iterationStart` → [iteration start](#iteration-start)
   * `iterations` → [iteration count](#iteration-count)
   * `duration` → [iteration duration](#iteration-duration)
   * `direction` → [playback direction](#playback-direction)
   * `easing` → easing function
6. If effect is [associated with an animation](#animation-effect-associated-animation),
   run the procedure to [update an animation’s finished state](#update-an-animations-finished-state)
   for its associated animation
   with the did seek flag set to false,
   and the synchronously notify flag set to false.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R111">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Constructing a KeyframeEffect with a numeric options argument must treat that number as the duration with all other timing members set to their default values.</description>
    <spec_quote>If options is a `KeyframeEffectOptions` object,
       :   Let timing input be options.

       Otherwise (if options is a `double`),
       :   Let timing input be a new `EffectTiming` object
           with all members set to their default values
           and `duration` set to options.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R112">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Constructing a KeyframeEffect from another KeyframeEffect source must copy its effect target, keyframes, composite operation, and all specified timing properties.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. Create a new `KeyframeEffect` object, effect.
    2. Set the following properties of effect
       using the corresponding values of source:

       * [effect target](#keyframe-effect-effect-target),
       * [keyframes](#keyframe),
       * [composite operation](#composite-operation),
         and
       * all specified timing properties:</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R113">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Setting KeyframeEffect.pseudoElement (or passing pseudoElement in options) with a legacy single-colon selector (':before', ':after', ':first-letter', or ':first-line') must normalize it to the equivalent two-colon selector.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. If value is one of the legacy Selectors Level 2 single-colon selectors
       (':before', ':after', ':first-letter', or ':first-line'), then
       return the equivalent two-colon selector (e.g. '::before').</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R114">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When processing an iterable keyframes argument (array-form), each yielded item must be processed as a keyframe object (with null or undefined items producing default keyframe values).</description>
    <spec_quote>If method is not undefined,
   :   1. Let iter be GetIterator(object, method).
       2. [Check the completion record](#check-the-completion-record) of iter.
       3. Repeat:

          1. Let next be IteratorStep(iter).
          2. [Check the completion record](#check-the-completion-record) of next.
          3. If next is false abort this loop.
          4. Let nextItem be IteratorValue(next).
          5. [Check the completion record](#check-the-completion-record) of nextItem.
          6. If Type(nextItem) is not `Undefined`, `Null` or `Object`,
             then throw a `TypeError` and abort these steps.
          7. Append to processed keyframes
             the result of running the procedure to
             [process a keyframe-like object](#process-a-keyframe-like-object)
             passing nextItem as the keyframe input
             with the allow lists flag set to false.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R115">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When processing a property-indexed keyframes argument (object-form), keyframes generated for each property must be sorted by computed keyframe offset and adjacent keyframes with equal computed offsets must be merged.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. Sort processed keyframes
          by the [computed keyframe offset](#computed-keyframe-offsets) of each [keyframe](#keyframe)
          in increasing order.
       4. Merge adjacent [keyframes](#keyframe) in processed keyframes
          when they have equal [computed keyframe offsets](#computed-keyframe-offsets).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R116">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When computing missing keyframe offsets, if there is more than one keyframe and the first has a null offset it must get 0, if the last has a null offset it must get 1, and any intermediate keyframes with null offsets must be evenly spaced between their nearest surrounding non-null offsets.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. If keyframes contains more than one [keyframe](#keyframe)
   and the [computed keyframe offset](#computed-keyframe-offsets)
   of the first keyframe in keyframes
   is null,
   set the computed keyframe offset of the first keyframe
   to 0.
3. If the [computed keyframe offset](#computed-keyframe-offsets)
   of the last [keyframe](#keyframe) in keyframes
   is null,
   set its computed keyframe offset to 1.
4. For each pair of [keyframes](#keyframe) A and B
   where:

   * A appears before B in keyframes, and
   * A and B have a [computed keyframe offset](#computed-keyframe-offsets)
     that is not null, and
   * all [keyframes](#keyframe) between A and B
     have a null [computed keyframe offset](#computed-keyframe-offsets),

   calculate the [computed keyframe offset](#computed-keyframe-offsets)
   of each [keyframe](#keyframe) between A and B
   as follows:

   1. Let offsetk be
      the [computed keyframe offset](#computed-keyframe-offsets) of a [keyframe](#keyframe) k.
   2. Let n be
      the number of keyframes *between* and including
      A and B minus 1.
   3. Let index refer to the position
      of keyframe in the sequence of keyframes between A and B
      such that the first keyframe after A has an index of 1.
   4. Set the [computed keyframe offset](#computed-keyframe-offsets) of keyframe to
      [offset](#offsetk)A +
      (offsetB −
      offsetA)
      × index / n.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R117">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Converting animation property names to IDL attribute names must keep custom property names verbatim, map CSS float to "cssFloat", map CSS offset to "cssOffset", and apply the CSSOM CSS property to IDL attribute algorithm for all other properties.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If property follows the <custom-property-name> production,
   return property.
2. If property refers to the CSS float property,
   return the string "cssFloat".
3. If property refers to the CSS offset property,
   return the string "cssOffset".
4. Otherwise, return the result of applying
   the CSS property to IDL attribute algorithm [[CSSOM]](#biblio-cssom "CSS Object Model (CSSOM)")
   to property.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R118">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>KeyframeEffect.getKeyframes() must return a sequence of keyframe objects containing offset, computedOffset, easing, composite, and serialized CSS string values keyed by each animated property's IDL attribute name.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. Set the
          `offset`,
          `computedOffset`,
          `easing`,
          and
          `composite`
          members of output keyframe
          to the respective
          [keyframe offset](#keyframe-offset),
          [computed keyframe offset](#computed-keyframe-offsets),
          keyframe-specific easing function,
          and [keyframe-specific composite operation](#keyframe-specific-composite-operation)
          values of keyframe.
       3. For each animation property-value pair declaration in keyframe,
          perform the following steps:

          1. Let property name be the result of applying the
             [animation property name to IDL attribute name](#animation-property-name-to-idl-attribute-name) algorithm
             to the property name of declaration.
          2. Let IDL value be the result
             of serializing the property value of declaration
             by passing declaration to
             the algorithm to serialize a CSS value [[CSSOM]](#biblio-cssom "CSS Object Model (CSSOM)").</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R119">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When computing property values in keyframes that depend on other properties on the target element (such as em units depending on an animated font-size), the computed values of dependencies must be calculated first.</description>
    <spec_quote>When [computing a property value](#compute-a-property-value),
the computed values of dependencies held by value
must be calculated *first*.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R120">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When expanding shorthand and logical properties in computed keyframes, conflicts must be resolved in order: longhands override shorthands, shorthands with fewer longhands override those with more, physical properties override logical properties, and equal-count shorthands resolve by ascending Unicode codepoint order of their IDL names.</description>
    <spec_quote>If conflicts arise when expanding shorthand properties
      or replacing logical properties with physical properties,
      apply the following rules in order until the conflict is resolved:

      1. Longhand properties override shorthand properties
         (e.g. border-top-color overrides border-top).
      2. Shorthand properties with fewer longhand components
         override those with more longhand components
         (e.g. border-top overrides border-color).
      3. Physical properties override logical properties.
      4. For shorthand properties with an equal number of longhand components,
         properties whose IDL name
         (see the CSS property to IDL attribute algorithm [[CSSOM]](#biblio-cssom "CSS Object Model (CSSOM)"))
         appears earlier when sorted in ascending order
         by the Unicode codepoints that make up each IDL name,
         override those who appear later.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R121">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When calculating the effect value for a target property that lacks a keyframe at computed offset 0 or 1, an implicit keyframe must be generated at that offset with the underlying value, replace composite operation, and linear easing.</description>
    <spec_quote>8. If there is no [keyframe](#keyframe) in property-specific keyframes
   with a [computed keyframe offset](#computed-keyframe-offsets) of 0,
   create a new keyframe
   with a computed keyframe offset of 0,
   a property value set to underlying value,
   a [keyframe-specific composite operation](#keyframe-specific-composite-operation)
   of [replace](#composite-operation-replace),
   and a [keyframe-specific easing function](#keyframe-specific-easing-function)
   of the linear easing function,
   and prepend it to the beginning of property-specific keyframes.
9. Similarly, if there is no [keyframe](#keyframe) in property-specific keyframes
   with a [computed keyframe offset](#computed-keyframe-offsets) of 1,
   create a new keyframe
   with a computed keyframe offset of 1,
   a property value set to underlying value,
   a [keyframe-specific composite operation](#keyframe-specific-composite-operation)
   of [replace](#composite-operation-replace),
   and a [keyframe-specific easing function](#keyframe-specific-easing-function)
   of the linear easing function,
   and append it to the end of property-specific keyframes.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R122">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>To compute the effect value between two interval endpoint keyframes, the user agent must compute interval distance as (iteration progress - start offset) / (end offset - start offset), transform it with the starting keyframe's easing function, and interpolate between the two keyframe values according to the target property's animation type.</description>
    <spec_quote>5. Let start offset be the [computed keyframe offset](#computed-keyframe-offsets)
   of the first keyframe in interval endpoints.
6. Let end offset be the [computed keyframe offset](#computed-keyframe-offsets)
   of last keyframe in interval endpoints.
7. Let interval distance be the result of evaluating
   `(iteration progress − start offset)
   / (end offset − start offset)`.
8. Let transformed distance be the result of evaluating
   the easing function associated with
   the first keyframe in interval endpoints
   passing interval distance as the input progress.
9. Return the result of applying
   the interpolation procedure defined
   by the [animation type](#animation-type) of the target property
   to the values of the target property
   specified on the two keyframes in interval endpoints,
   taking the first such value as Vstart
   and the second as Vend
   and using transformed distance
   as the interpolation parameter p.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R123">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Registered custom properties with a corresponding computed value type must animate by computed value, while unregistered custom properties or those without a corresponding computed value type must animate discretely.</description>
    <spec_quote>For custom properties registered using
the `registerProperty()` method for the current global object,
the [animation type](#animation-type) is [by computed value](#by-computed-value),
derived from the type used in the property’s syntax definition.
Where there is no computed value type that corresponds
to the property’s specified syntax
(e.g. when the syntax is the universal syntax definition)
or when the custom property is not registered,
the animation type is [discrete](#discrete).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R124">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Multiple keyframe effects targeting the same property must be sorted in the effect stack by inter-class composite order, then class-specific composite order, and finally by the creation order of their associated animations in the global animation list.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. Sort A and B
   by applying the following conditions in turn
   until the order is resolved,

   1. If A and B’s [associated animations](#animation-effect-associated-animation) differ
      by [class](#animation-class),
      sort by any inter-class composite order
      as defined for the corresponding classes.
   2. If A and B are still not sorted,
      sort by any [class](#animation-class)-specific composite order
      defined by the common class of A and B’s
      [associated animations](#animation-effect-associated-animation).
   3. If A and B are still not sorted,
      sort by the position of their [associated animations](#animation-effect-associated-animation)
      in the [global animation list](#global-animation-list).

[Animation effects](#animation-effect) that sort earlier have *lower* composite order.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R125">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Applying animated values to a CSS target property must evaluate the property's effect stack in composite order starting from its base computed value (in the absence of animations) and insert the resulting composited value into the CSS cascade at the level of the top effect's animation class (Animation Origin by default).</description>
    <spec_quote>1. Calculate the base value of the property
   as the value generated for that property
   by finding the computed value for that property
   in the absence of animations.
2. Establish the [effect stack](#effect-stack) for the property
   (see [§ 5.4.2 The effect stack](#the-effect-stack)).
3. Calculate the [composited value](#composited-value) of the [effect stack](#effect-stack)
   passing in the base value of the property
   as the initial [underlying value](#underlying-value)
   (see [§ 5.4.3 Calculating the result of an effect stack](#calculating-the-result-of-an-effect-stack)).
4. Insert the [composited value](#composited-value) into the CSS cascade
   at the level defined for the [class](#animation-class) of
   the [animation](#concept-animation) [associated with](#animation-effect-associated-animation)
   the effect at the top of the [effect stack](#effect-stack)
   established for the [target property](#target-property).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R126">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>For every property targeted by a current or in-effect animation effect whose animation does not have a replace state of removed, the user agent must act as if will-change on the effect target includes that property.</description>
    <spec_quote>For every property targeted by at least one [animation effect](#animation-effect)
that is [current](#current) or [in effect](#in-effect),
and which is associated with an [animation](#concept-animation)
whose [replace state](#replace-state) is *not* [removed](#removed-replace-state),
the user agent must act as if
the will-change property [[css-will-change-1]](#biblio-css-will-change-1 "CSS Will Change Module Level 1") on the [effect target](#keyframe-effect-effect-target)
includes the property.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R127">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When a replaceable, active, finished, in-effect scripted animation has all of its targeted properties overridden by higher-composite-order replaceable animations, its replace state must be set to removed (excluding it from effect stacks) and a remove AnimationPlaybackEvent must be queued.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. Set animation’s [replace state](#replace-state) to [removed](#removed-replace-state).
2. Create an `AnimationPlaybackEvent`, removeEvent.
3. Set removeEvent’s `type` attribute to [remove](#remove-event).
4. Set removeEvent’s `currentTime` attribute
   to the [current time](#animation-current-time) of animation.
5. Set removeEvent’s `timelineTime` attribute
   to the [current time](#timeline-current-time)
   of the [timeline](#timeline) with which animation is associated.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R128">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Calling animation.persist() must set the animation's replace state to persisted so it is not automatically removed when overridden by newer animations.</description>
    <spec_quote>`void persist()`
:   Sets this animation’s [replace state](#replace-state)
    to [persisted](#persisted-replace-state).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R129">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Calling animation.commitStyles() must calculate each targeted physical longhand property's value from the partial effect stack up to the animation's composite order using endpoint-inclusive timing (including the animation's own effects even if removed), write the declarations to the target element's inline style attribute, and trigger a style change event.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. Let effect value be the result of calculating
         the result of partialEffectStack for property
         using target’s computed style
         (see [§ 5.4.3 Calculating the result of an effect stack](#calculating-the-result-of-an-effect-stack)) and
         setting the [endpoint-inclusive active interval](#endpoint-inclusive-active-interval) flag
         to true
         when calculating the animation effect phase
         (see [§ 4.6.6 Animation effect phases and states](#animation-effect-phases-and-states)).
      5. Set a CSS declaration of property for effect value
         in inline style.
   6. Update style attribute for inline style.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R130">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Calling Element.getAnimations(options) must trigger a style change event and return the relevant animations (current or in-effect and not removed) targeting the element (or specified pseudoElement, or subtree if subtree is true), sorted in composite order.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. If `options` is passed
       with `subtree` set to true,
       then return the set of [relevant animations for a subtree](#relevant-animations-for-a-subtree) of target.
       Otherwise, return the set of [relevant animations](#relevant-animations) for target.

    The list returned by the above algorithm is sorted using
    the composite order described for the associated [animations](#concept-animation)
    of effects in [§ 5.4.2 The effect stack](#the-effect-stack).

    Calling this method triggers
    a style change event for the [target element](#effect-target-target-element).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R131">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Calling document.getAnimations() or shadowRoot.getAnimations() must trigger a style change event and return the relevant animations for the document or shadow root's subtree sorted in composite order.</description>
    <spec_quote>`sequence<Animation> getAnimations()`
:   Returns the set of [relevant animations for a subtree](#relevant-animations-for-a-subtree)
    for the document or shadow root
    on which this method is called.

    The returned list is sorted
    using the composite order described for the associated [animations](#concept-animation)
    of effects in [§ 5.4.2 The effect stack](#the-effect-stack).

    Calling this method triggers a style change event for the document.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R132">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Changes made to any part of the Web Animations model must immediately update the timing model and dependent styles, while invoking Web Animations API methods, constructors, getters, or setters (unless otherwise specified) must not produce a style change event.</description>
    <spec_quote>Changes made to any part of the model
cause the entire timing model to be updated
and any dependent style.

Unless otherwise stated,
invoking the methods or constructors,
or getting or setting the members
of interfaces defined in the [Web Animations API](#web-animations-api)
does *not* produce a style change event.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R133">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Setting an animation's `currentTime` to `null` (an unresolved time value) while its `currentTime` is currently resolved must throw a `TypeError` and abort the operation.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If seek time is an [unresolved](#unresolved) time value,
   then perform the following steps.

   1. If the [current time](#animation-current-time) is resolved,
      then throw a TypeError.
   2. Abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R134">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.play()` (with auto-rewind enabled) when the animation's effective playback rate is negative, its associated effect end is positive infinity, and its current time is unresolved, less than or equal to zero, or greater than the associated effect end must throw an `InvalidStateError` `DOMException` and abort playback.</description>
    <spec_quote>If animation’s [effective playback rate](#effective-playback-rate) < 0, and animation’s [current time](#animation-current-time) is *either*: * [unresolved](#unresolved), or * less than or equal to zero, or * greater than [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end),
   :   If [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end) is positive infinity,
       :   throw an "`InvalidStateError`" `DOMException`
           and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R135">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.pause()` when the animation's current time is unresolved, its playback rate is negative, and its associated effect end is positive infinity must throw an `InvalidStateError` `DOMException` and abort pausing.</description>
    <spec_quote>5. If the animation’s [current time](#animation-current-time) is [unresolved](#unresolved),
   perform the steps according to the first matching condition below:

   If animation’s [playback rate](#playback-rate) is ≥ 0,
   :   Set seek time to zero.

   Otherwise,
   :   If [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end) for animation is positive infinity,
       :   throw an "`InvalidStateError`" `DOMException`
           and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R136">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.finish()` when the animation's effective playback rate is zero must throw an `InvalidStateError` `DOMException` and abort the operation.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If animation’s [effective playback rate](#effective-playback-rate) is zero,
   or if animation’s effective playback rate > 0
   and [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end) is infinity,
   throw an "`InvalidStateError`" `DOMException`
   and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R137">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.finish()` when the animation's effective playback rate is greater than zero and its associated effect end is positive infinity must throw an `InvalidStateError` `DOMException` and abort the operation.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If animation’s [effective playback rate](#effective-playback-rate) is zero,
   or if animation’s effective playback rate > 0
   and [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end) is infinity,
   throw an "`InvalidStateError`" `DOMException`
   and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R138">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.cancel()` on an animation whose `playState` is not `"idle"` must reject its current `finished` promise with an `AbortError` `DOMException`.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If animation’s [play state](#animation-play-state) is *not* [idle](#play-state-idle),
   perform the following steps:

   1. Run the procedure to [reset an animation’s pending tasks](#animation-reset-an-animations-pending-tasks)
      on animation.
   2. Reject the [current finished promise](#current-finished-promise)
      with a `DOMException` named "`AbortError`".</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R139">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>When canceling a non-idle animation rejects its current `finished` promise, the promise's `[[PromiseIsHandled]]` internal slot must be set to `true` so that an unhandled rejection is not reported.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. Set the [[PromiseIsHandled]] internal slot
      of the [current finished promise](#current-finished-promise)
      to true.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R140">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.cancel()` on an animation that has a pending play task or pending pause task must reject its current `ready` promise with an `AbortError` `DOMException`.</description>
    <spec_quote>5. Reject
   animation’s [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise)
   with a `DOMException` named "`AbortError`".</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R141">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>When resetting an animation's pending tasks rejects its current `ready` promise, the promise's `[[PromiseIsHandled]]` internal slot must be set to `true` so that an unhandled rejection is not reported.</description>
    <spec_quote>6. Set the [[PromiseIsHandled]] internal slot of animation’s
   [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise) to true.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R142">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.reverse()` when the animation has no associated timeline or its associated timeline is inactive must throw an `InvalidStateError` `DOMException` and abort the operation.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If there is no [timeline](#timeline) associated with animation,
   or the associated timeline is [inactive](#inactive-timeline)
   throw an "`InvalidStateError`" `DOMException`
   and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R143">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>If invoking the play procedure during `Animation.reverse()` throws an exception (such as when the inverted playback rate is negative with an infinite effect end and unresolved or non-positive current time), `reverse()` must restore the animation's pending playback rate to its original value and propagate the exception.</description>
    <spec_quote>If the steps to [play an animation](#play-an-animation) throw an exception,
   set animation’s [pending playback rate](#pending-playback-rate)
   to original pending playback rate
   and propagate the exception.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R144">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.commitStyles()` when any effect target is not an element capable of having a `style` attribute (such as a pseudo-element or an element without style attribute support) must throw a `NoModificationAllowedError` `DOMException` and abort the operation.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If target is not an element capable of having
      a style attribute [[CSS-STYLE-ATTR]](#biblio-css-style-attr "CSS Style Attributes")
      (for example, it is a pseudo-element
      or is an element in a document format
      for which style attributes are not defined)
      throw a "`NoModificationAllowedError`" `DOMException`
      and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R145">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.commitStyles()` when any effect target is not being rendered after applying pending style changes (e.g., disconnected or within a `display: none` subtree) must throw an `InvalidStateError` `DOMException` and abort the operation.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. If, after applying any pending style changes,
      target is not being rendered,
      throw an "`InvalidStateError`" `DOMException`
      and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R146">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Updating an `AnimationEffect`'s timing (via `updateTiming()`, `KeyframeEffect` construction, or `Element.animate()`) with an `iterationStart` value less than zero must throw a `TypeError` and abort without applying timing changes.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. If the `iterationStart` member of input
   exists and is less than zero,
   throw a `TypeError` and abort this procedure.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R147">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Updating an `AnimationEffect`'s timing with an `iterations` value that is less than zero or `NaN` must throw a `TypeError` and abort without applying timing changes.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. If the `iterations` member of input exists,
   and is less than zero or is the value `NaN`,
   throw a `TypeError` and abort this procedure.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R148">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Updating an `AnimationEffect`'s timing with a numeric `duration` value that is less than zero or `NaN` must throw a `TypeError` and abort without applying timing changes.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. If the `duration` member of input exists,
   and is less than zero, is the value `NaN`,
   or is a string other than the lowercase `auto`,
   throw a `TypeError` and abort this procedure.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R149">
