  <requirement id="R204">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>A document timeline associated with a `Document` that is not an HTML active document must be inactive (returning `null` for `currentTime`).</description>
    <spec_quote>A [document timeline](#document-timeline) that is associated
with a `Document` that is not an active document
is also considered to be [inactive](#inactive-timeline).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R205">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>A document's default document timeline (`document.timeline`) must persist as the same instance for the lifetime of the document, including across calls to `document.open()`.</description>
    <spec_quote>The [default document timeline](#document-default-document-timeline) is unique to each document
and persists for the lifetime of the document,
including calls to document.open() [[HTML]](#biblio-html "HTML Standard").</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R206">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>During the `update animations and send events` procedure, the user agent must perform a microtask checkpoint before dispatching queued animation events so that promise microtasks from timeline updates run prior to animation event listeners.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. Perform a microtask checkpoint.

   Note: This is to ensure that any microtasks queued up
   as a result of resolving or rejecting Promise objects
   as part of updating timelines in the previous step,
   run their callbacks prior to dispatching animation events.
4. Let events to dispatch be a copy of doc’s [pending animation event queue](#pending-animation-event-queue).
5. Clear doc’s [pending animation event queue](#pending-animation-event-queue).
6. Perform a stable sort of the [animation events](#animation-events) in events to dispatch
   as follows:

   1. Sort the events by their [scheduled event time](#scheduled-event-time)
      such that events that were scheduled to occur earlier
      sort before events scheduled to occur later,
      and events whose scheduled event time is [unresolved](#unresolved)
      sort before events with a resolved
      scheduled event time.
   2. Within events with equal [scheduled event times](#scheduled-event-time),
      sort by their [composite order](#animation-composite-order).

      Note: The purpose of sorting events is to ensure that, as best possible,
      even on devices with differing capabilities
      and hence different frame rates,
      events are dispatched in a consistent order.

      Note: The requirement for the sort to be a stable sort
      is because sometimes multiple events can be queued
      with the same scheduled event time.
      For example, a CSS animation with a duration of zero would dispatch
      both an `animationstart` and an `animationend` event
      with the same scheuled event time,
      and the order of these events should be preserved.
7. Dispatch each of the events in events to dispatch at their
   corresponding target using the order established in the previous step.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R207">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When an animation finishes without a document for timing, the user agent must queue a task on the HTML DOM manipulation task source to dispatch the `finish` event at the animation.</description>
    <spec_quote>7. If animation has a [document for timing](#animation-document-for-timing),
         then append finishEvent
         to its document for timing’s [pending animation event queue](#pending-animation-event-queue)
         along with its target, animation.
         For the [scheduled event time](#scheduled-event-time),
         use the result of
         [converting](#animation-time-to-origin-relative-time)
         animation’s [associated effect end](#associated-effect-end)
         to an origin-relative time.

         Otherwise,
         queue a task to dispatch finishEvent at animation.
         The task source for this task is
         the DOM manipulation task source.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R208">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When canceling a non-idle animation, the user agent must set the `[[PromiseIsHandled]]` internal slot of the rejected `current finished promise` to `true` so that an unhandled promise rejection is not reported.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. Reject the [current finished promise](#current-finished-promise)
      with a `DOMException` named "`AbortError`".
   3. Set the [[PromiseIsHandled]] internal slot
      of the [current finished promise](#current-finished-promise)
      to true.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R209">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When an animation is canceled without a document for timing, the user agent must queue a task on the HTML DOM manipulation task source to dispatch the `cancel` event at the animation.</description>
    <spec_quote>10. If animation has a [document for timing](#animation-document-for-timing),
       then append cancelEvent to
       its document for timing’s [pending animation event queue](#pending-animation-event-queue)
       along with its target, animation.
       If animation is associated with an [active timeline](#active-timeline)
       that defines a procedure to
       [convert
       timeline times to origin-relative time](#timeline-time-to-origin-relative-time),
       let the [scheduled event time](#scheduled-event-time) be
       the result of applying that procedure to timeline time.
       Otherwise, the scheduled event time is
       an [unresolved](#unresolved) [time value](#time-value).

       Otherwise,
       queue a task to dispatch cancelEvent at animation.
       The task source for this task is
       the DOM manipulation task source.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R210">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When resetting an animation's pending play or pause tasks, the user agent must set the `[[PromiseIsHandled]]` internal slot of the rejected `current ready promise` to `true` so that an unhandled promise rejection is not reported.</description>
    <spec_quote>5. Reject
   animation’s [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise)
   with a `DOMException` named "`AbortError`".
6. Set the [[PromiseIsHandled]] internal slot of animation’s
   [current ready promise](#current-ready-promise) to true.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R211">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>The document's pending animation event queue and sorting order must integrate Web Animations playback events together with events from CSS Transitions and CSS Animations.</description>
    <spec_quote>Animation events include
the [animation playback events](#animation-playback-events) defined in this specification
as well as the events from CSS transitions [[CSS-TRANSITIONS-1]](#biblio-css-transitions-1 "CSS Transitions Module Level 1")
and events from CSS animations [[CSS-ANIMATIONS-1]](#biblio-css-animations-1 "CSS Animations Level 1").</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R212">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>For CSS custom properties registered via `registerProperty()` in the current global object with a syntax corresponding to a computed value type, the animation type must be by computed value derived from the property's registered syntax definition.</description>
    <spec_quote>For custom properties registered using
the `registerProperty()` method for the current global object,
the [animation type](#animation-type) is [by computed value](#by-computed-value),
derived from the type used in the property’s syntax definition.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R213">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When a CSS custom property is unregistered or its registered syntax has no corresponding computed value type (such as the universal syntax definition), its animation type must be discrete.</description>
    <spec_quote>Where there is no computed value type that corresponds
to the property’s specified syntax
(e.g. when the syntax is the universal syntax definition)
or when the custom property is not registered,
the animation type is [discrete](#discrete).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R214">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When computing property values for keyframes on a target element, the computed values of any CSS property dependencies referenced by a value (such as `font-size` for `em` units) must be calculated first.</description>
    <spec_quote>When [computing a property value](#compute-a-property-value),
the computed values of dependencies held by value
must be calculated *first*.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R215">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When computing keyframes, CSS logical properties must be converted into their equivalent physical properties based on the effect target's computed `writing-mode` and/or `direction`.</description>
    <spec_quote>For logical properties [[CSS-LOGICAL-1]](#biblio-css-logical-1 "CSS Logical Properties and Values Module Level 1"),
        add the equivalent physical properties [[CSS-WRITING-MODES-4]](#biblio-css-writing-modes-4 "CSS Writing Modes Level 4")
        based on the computed value of writing-mode and/or direction
        for the [effect target](#keyframe-effect-effect-target).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R216">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When expanding logical properties in a keyframe causes a conflict with a physical property targeting the same longhand property, the physical property must override the logical property.</description>
    <spec_quote>If conflicts arise when expanding shorthand properties
      or replacing logical properties with physical properties,
      apply the following rules in order until the conflict is resolved:

      1. Longhand properties override shorthand properties
         (e.g. border-top-color overrides border-top).
      2. Shorthand properties with fewer longhand components
         override those with more longhand components
         (e.g. border-top overrides border-color).
      3. Physical properties override logical properties.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R217">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>Applying a composited animation value to a CSS target property must insert the specified value into the CSS cascade at the level defined for the class of the highest-composite-order animation in the effect stack, defaulting to the Animation Origin of the cascade.</description>
    <spec_quote>Applying a [composited value](#composited-value) to a [target property](#target-property)
is achieved by adding a specified value to the CSS cascade.

The level of the cascade to which this specified value is added
depends on the [class](#animation-class) of the [animation](#concept-animation)
[associated with](#animation-effect-associated-animation)
the effect with the highest composite order in the [effect stack](#effect-stack)
for a given property.
By default, the specified value is added to
the Animation Origin of the cascade. [[CSS-CASCADE-3]](#biblio-css-cascade-3 "CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 3")</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R218">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>CSS animations with an owning element and CSS transitions with an owning element must not be considered replaceable and must not be automatically removed by the replaced animations procedure.</description>
    <spec_quote>An [animation](#concept-animation) is
replaceable
if *all* of the following conditions are true:

* The existence of the [animation](#concept-animation) is *not* prescribed by markup.
  That is, it is *not*
  a CSS animation with an owning element,
  nor a CSS transition with an owning element.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R219">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When an animation is automatically removed without a document for timing, the user agent must queue a task on the HTML DOM manipulation task source to dispatch the `remove` event at the animation.</description>
    <spec_quote>6. If animation has a [document for timing](#animation-document-for-timing),
   then append removeEvent
   to its document for timing’s [pending animation event queue](#pending-animation-event-queue)
   along with its target, animation.
   For the [scheduled event time](#scheduled-event-time),
   use the result of applying the procedure to convert
   [timeline time to origin-relative time](#timeline-time-to-origin-relative-time)
   to the [current time](#timeline-current-time) of the [timeline](#timeline)
   with which animation is associated.

   Otherwise,
   queue a task to dispatch removeEvent at animation.
   The task source for this task is
   the DOM manipulation task source.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R220">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>For every CSS property targeted by at least one current or in-effect animation effect whose animation does not have a replace state of `removed`, the user agent must apply the same side effects as if the CSS `will-change` property on the effect target included that property.</description>
    <spec_quote>For every property targeted by at least one [animation effect](#animation-effect)
that is [current](#current) or [in effect](#in-effect),
and which is associated with an [animation](#concept-animation)
whose [replace state](#replace-state) is *not* [removed](#removed-replace-state),
the user agent must act as if
the will-change property [[css-will-change-1]](#biblio-css-will-change-1 "CSS Will Change Module Level 1") on the [effect target](#keyframe-effect-effect-target)
includes the property.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R221">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>`Animation.commitStyles()` must be annotated with `[CEReactions]` so that custom element reactions are invoked when updating the target element's `style` attribute.</description>
    <spec_quote>[CEReactions]
  undefined commitStyles();</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R222">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>`Animation.commitStyles()` must write the current computed effect values of the animation's effects to the corresponding effect targets' inline `style` attribute.</description>
    <spec_quote>Writes the current [effect values](#effect-value)
    produced by this animation’s [animation effects](#animation-effect)
    to their corresponding [effect targets](#keyframe-effect-effect-target)' inline style
    using the [commit computed styles](#commit-computed-styles) procedure.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R223">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>Calling `Animation.commitStyles()` must trigger a style change event.</description>
    <spec_quote>Unlike most other methods defined on this interface,
    calling this method *does* trigger a style change event
    (see [§ 6.13 Model liveness](#model-liveness)).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R224">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>If any effect target is not an element capable of having a CSS `style` attribute (such as a pseudo-element or an element without style attribute support), `Animation.commitStyles()` must throw a `NoModificationAllowedError` `DOMException`.</description>
    <spec_quote>If target is not an element capable of having
      a style attribute [[CSS-STYLE-ATTR]](#biblio-css-style-attr "CSS Style Attributes")
      (for example, it is a pseudo-element
      or is an element in a document format
      for which style attributes are not defined)
      throw a "`NoModificationAllowedError`" `DOMException`
      and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R225">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>If, after applying pending style changes, any effect target is not being rendered according to HTML, `Animation.commitStyles()` must throw an `InvalidStateError` `DOMException`.</description>
    <spec_quote>If, after applying any pending style changes,
      target is not being rendered,
      throw an "`InvalidStateError`" `DOMException`
      and abort these steps.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R226">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>For `Animation.commitStyles()`, a connected element with `display: contents` that is not part of a `display: none` subtree must be treated as being rendered.</description>
    <spec_quote>For the purpose of this procedure,
      we assume that an element with display: contents
      that otherwise would have associated layout boxes
      (i.e. it is connected
      and not part of a display: none subtree)
      *is* being rendered.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R227">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>Setting a target pseudo-selector to a non-null string that is an invalid CSS `<pseudo-element-selector>` must throw a `SyntaxError` `DOMException` and leave the target pseudo-selector unchanged.</description>
    <spec_quote>If value is not `null`
       and is an invalid <pseudo-element-selector>,

       1. Throw a `DOMException`
          with error name "`SyntaxError`".
       2. Abort.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R228">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When parsing a target pseudo-selector, legacy Selectors Level 2 single-colon selectors (`:before`, `:after`, `:first-letter`, `:first-line`) must be normalized to their equivalent two-colon selectors.</description>
    <spec_quote>If value is one of the legacy Selectors Level 2 single-colon selectors
       (':before', ':after', ':first-letter', or ':first-line'), then
       return the equivalent two-colon selector (e.g. '::before').</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R229">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When `KeyframeEffect.getKeyframes()` is called on an effect associated with a `CSSAnimation` whose keyframes have not been replaced via `setKeyframes()`, it must return keyframes derived from the effect's computed keyframes.</description>
    <spec_quote>If this [keyframe effect](#keyframe-effect) is associated with a `CSSAnimation`, and its [keyframes](#keyframe) have not been replaced by a successful call to `setKeyframes()`,
       :   the [computed keyframes](#computed-keyframes) for this [keyframe effect](#keyframe-effect).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R230">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When `KeyframeEffect.getKeyframes()` outputs keyframe declarations, each property value must be serialized using the CSSOM algorithm to serialize a CSS value.</description>
    <spec_quote>Let IDL value be the result
             of serializing the property value of declaration
             by passing declaration to
             the algorithm to serialize a CSS value [[CSSOM]](#biblio-cssom "CSS Object Model (CSSOM)").</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R231">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When mapping an animation property name to an IDL attribute name, custom property names must remain unchanged, `float` must map to `"cssFloat"`, `offset` must map to `"cssOffset"`, and all other properties must use the CSSOM CSS property to IDL attribute algorithm.</description>
    <spec_quote>The animation property name to IDL attribute name algorithm
for property
is as follows:

1. If property follows the <custom-property-name> production,
   return property.
2. If property refers to the CSS float property,
   return the string "cssFloat".
3. If property refers to the CSS offset property,
   return the string "cssOffset".
4. Otherwise, return the result of applying
   the CSS property to IDL attribute algorithm [[CSSOM]](#biblio-cssom "CSS Object Model (CSSOM)")
   to property.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R232">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When mapping a keyframe IDL attribute name to an animation property name, custom property names must remain unchanged, `"cssFloat"` must map to the CSS `float` property, `"cssOffset"` must map to the CSS `offset` property, and all other attributes must use the CSSOM IDL attribute to CSS property algorithm.</description>
    <spec_quote>The IDL attribute name to animation property name algorithm
for attribute
is as follows:

1. If attribute conforms to the <custom-property-name> production,
   return attribute.
2. If attribute is the string "cssFloat", then return
   an animation property representing the CSS float property.
3. If attribute is the string "cssOffset", then return
   an animation property representing the CSS offset property.
4. Otherwise, return the result of applying
   the IDL attribute to CSS property algorithm [[CSSOM]](#biblio-cssom "CSS Object Model (CSSOM)")
   to attribute.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R233">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>Calling `Element.getAnimations()` must trigger a style change event for the target element so that pending animation-related style changes are reflected in the returned list.</description>
    <spec_quote>Calling this method triggers
    a style change event for the [target element](#effect-target-target-element).
    As a result, the returned list reflects the state
    *after* applying any pending style changes to animation
    such as changes to animation-related style properties
    that have yet to be processed.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R234">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>The DOM `Document` interface must be extended with a readonly `timeline` attribute of type `DocumentTimeline`.</description>
    <spec_quote>partial interface Document {
    readonly attribute DocumentTimeline timeline;
};</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R235">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>The DOM `DocumentOrShadowRoot` mixin must expose `getAnimations()`, returning the relevant animations for the subtree of the `Document` or `ShadowRoot` on which it is called.</description>
    <spec_quote>`sequence<Animation> getAnimations()`
:   Returns the set of [relevant animations for a subtree](#relevant-animations-for-a-subtree)
    for the document or shadow root
    on which this method is called.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R236">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>Calling `getAnimations()` on a `Document` or `ShadowRoot` must trigger a style change event for the document so that pending animation-related style changes are reflected in the returned list.</description>
    <spec_quote>Calling this method triggers a style change event for the document.
    As a result, the returned list reflects the state
    *after* applying any pending style changes to animation
    such as changes to animation-related style properties
    that have yet to be processed.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R237">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>The DOM `Element` interface must include the `Animatable` interface mixin.</description>
    <spec_quote>Element includes Animatable;</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R238">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>Changes made to any part of the Web Animations model must immediately update the entire timing model and any dependent CSS styles.</description>
    <spec_quote>Changes made to any part of the model
cause the entire timing model to be updated
and any dependent style.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R239">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>Unless otherwise stated by the specification, invoking Web Animations API methods or constructors, or getting or setting its interface members, must not produce a style change event.</description>
    <spec_quote>Unless otherwise stated,
invoking the methods or constructors,
or getting or setting the members
of interfaces defined in the [Web Animations API](#web-animations-api)
does *not* produce a style change event.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
</requirements_list>
